text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point and lowers the points of every other member by 0.3. In the same way, every token another member keeps in their own account lowers your points by 0.3.
- Each token in the group account pays you 0.3 points and does not change any other member's points.
- Every round, every member also receives 18 points, whatever anyone does.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a public goods game with a negative externality to weigh: keeping a token private gives me +1 but costs each other member 0.3, for a net social value of +0.1 per token, while putting a token in the group account gives me only 0.3 with no effect on others. I'm comparing the social efficiency of private versus group contributions.

Taking the literal reading, the token pays only me 0.3 and leaves others unchanged, so private holding (1 point) strictly dominates contributing (0.3 point) individually, even though social surplus is higher with contribution (0.3 vs 0.1 net). That makes full privatization the dominant strategy and Nash equilibrium, despite being socially suboptimal — a classic public goods tension, though without the usual multiplier-shared structure.

Keeping tokens dominates individually since it nets me +0.7 more than contributing, meaning the Nash equilibrium is to keep everything (zero to group). But socially, contributing produces a higher total payoff (0.3 per token) than keeping (0.1 per token), creating a clear free-rider dilemma. Since this is repeated over 10 rounds and I only observe the group total, I'm weighing whether to start cooperatively despite the individual cost.

I'll go with contributing 10 of my 20 tokens as a moderate opening move, signaling some cooperation while limiting my exposure if others defect.
